explanation: The tool sequence was appropriate, but the image prompts substituted abstract strokes for meaningful tasks and omitted lettering:true, allowing garbled interface text instead of a clear app demonstration. The models also disregarded the requests for no words and a white closing band; text-overlay itself was appropriate for the name over a clip. Silence was handled by the default audio removal, so the grader should not mark it missing merely because still frames cannot verify it.
better_chain: image (lettering:true; blue-and-white messy list with a few short, readable tasks) → image-edit (lettering:true; organize those same tasks into a timed daily plan) → image-to-video (short, gentle transition between the screens; discard generated audio) → assemble (readable original-screen holds around the transition, totaling exactly 8 seconds at 16:9, silent) → text-overlay (ClearDay during the final two seconds, with a restrained, explicitly sized white band)

steps.issue: The image tool was appropriate, but abstract lines weakened the service demonstration. Use lettering:true and a few meaningful task labels rather than relying on a no-text prompt to prevent invented interface words.

Editing the starting screen was the right way to preserve continuity, but the prompt retained abstract task descriptions and omitted lettering:true to replace the existing gibberish with readable daily-plan labels.
Correctly uses the messy and organized screens as start and end frames, specifies an eight-second landscape transition, and requests a closing hold. Generated audio is dropped by default.

Plain closing text over a clip is an appropriate use of text-overlay. The exact name, timing, position, and colors were specified; the reported dark-gray rectangle contradicts those settings rather than proving a wrong-tool choice.
